cards.text: Meet Zephaniah, a prophet in the days of Josiah, king of Judah (Zephaniah 1:1). He just finished warning that the great Day of the LORD is near, near and coming quickly (Zephaniah 1:14). Now he calls out to a shameful nation: “Gather yourselves, gather together.”

cards.question: Zephaniah tells the shameful nation to gather together. What does he want them to gather before?

answers.text: The Day of the LORD's anger

cards.text: Three times in one verse he says “before”: before the decree takes effect, before the burning anger of the LORD, before the Day of the LORD's anger. Friend, that's not a gentle reminder, that's an oven timer going BEEP BEEP BEEP.
Then the prophet turns to all the humble of the earth, the ones who carry out His justice.

cards.question: What does Zephaniah tell all the humble of the earth to do?
Zephaniah promises the humble they will surely be sheltered on the day of the LORD's anger.

cards.text: He tells them to seek righteousness and seek humility, and says, “Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD's anger.” Not “guaranteed,” not “money back,” just perhaps, and somehow that one word makes me stand up straighter on my gold base.
Then Zephaniah says “For,” and names four cities: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron.

cards.question: Gaza will be ___, and Ashkelon left in ruins.

cards.text: Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted. NOON, friend, no sneaking out at midnight, they get driven out in broad daylight.
Then comes a “Woe” for the dwellers of the seacoast, the nation of the Cherethites, and the word of the LORD is against Canaan.

cards.question: The word of the LORD is against Canaan on the seacoast. Whose land is it?

cards.text: Then the LORD says, “I will destroy you, and no one will be left.” So what happens to a coastline with nobody on it?

cards.question: The emptied seacoast becomes a land of pastures, with wells for shepherds and folds for sheep.

cards.text: Cities on the coast, turned into sheep country. That's pulling into the office parking lot Monday morning and it's just SHEEP, as far as you can see.

cards.question: Zephaniah says the coast will end up belonging to someone. Who?
The remnant of Judah will lie down in the evening among the houses of Ashkelon.
They can rest there, for the LORD their God will attend to them and ___ their captives.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks about Moab and the Ammonites, two nations that came from Lot's sons (Genesis 19:37-38). He says, “I have heard the reproach of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites.”

cards.question: What did Moab and the Ammonites do to the LORD's people?

answers.text: Taunted them and threatened their borders
Traded with them and shared their land
Fled from them and left their towns

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says, “as surely as I live.” And He compares these two nations to a famous pair of cities from Lot's day (Genesis 19:24-25).

cards.question: Moab will be like ___ and the Ammonites like ___.

cards.text: He says they'll be “a place of weeds and salt pits, a perpetual wasteland.” Perpetual, friend, that's not a fixer-upper, that's a FOR SALE sign nobody EVER takes down.

cards.question: The LORD says the remnant of His people will plunder Moab and the Ammonites.
Zephaniah says Moab and the Ammonites get all this in return for something. What?

cards.text: The LORD will be terrifying to them when He starves all the gods of the earth. Every one of those gods is about to find out what the back of a junk drawer feels like, and trust me, I've got the dust to prove it.

cards.question: Then the nations of every shore will ___ Him, each in its own place.

cards.text: Next comes one short line: “You too, O Cushites, will be slain by My sword.” Then the LORD will stretch out His hand against the north.

cards.question: The LORD stretches out His hand against the north. Which nation will He destroy?

cards.text: And He goes after Nineveh, the city Assyria's founder built (Genesis 10:11). Yes, THAT Nineveh, the one Jonah tried so hard not to visit (Jonah 1:2-3).

cards.question: The LORD will make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as a desert.
Once Nineveh is a dry desolation, who moves in?

cards.text: Owls roost atop her pillars, their calls sound from the window, desolation lies on the threshold, and the beams of cedar are exposed. That's not a city anymore, friend, that's a nature documentary where the narrator is whispering.
Then Zephaniah calls her “This carefree city that dwells securely.” Feet up on the desk, phone on silent, not a worry in the world.

cards.question: What does this carefree city think to herself?

answers.text: That no one else compares to her

cards.question: People passing by the ruined city stop to weep for her.

cards.text: Instead everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist, and the city that said “I am it” is a resting place for beasts. Friend, that's every cookie that ever bragged it couldn't burn.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "crowned" is a silly fit for a city in a line about ruin. It isn't the same kind of thing as "abandoned," so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card only restates Zephaniah 2:6, which card 14 already covered ("Cities on the coast, turned into sheep country"), and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward, and the joke doesn't ride along on new passage content.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The setup says the comparison is to "a famous pair of cities from Lot's day." That rules out the wrong answers on card 4: Jericho and Samaria aren't from Lot's day, and Babel isn't a city tied to Lot. Only Sodom and Gomorrah are left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This is the first time the Cushites appear, and the card doesn't say simply who they are.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card calls Nineveh "the city Assyria's founder built" and cites Genesis 10:11. That verse says only that he went forth into Assyria and built Nineveh. It never calls him Assyria's founder.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The card has four things happening before the joke: owls roost on her pillars, their calls sound from the window, desolation lies on the threshold, and the cedar beams are exposed.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.
